defect_observations.observation: Queue and packet evidence for this file is stale: recorded sha256 8c4d7dce... (queue) / 8C4D7DCE... (packet) differs from current 714b8f45... (changed in commit 55b51f69). Recorded exact_current_text no longer matches for ED26-P15-CH-integration-expectation-C018 and -C020, and recorded body_lines are now C018 378-407 (was 378-405), C019 409-424 (was 407-422), C020 426-444 (was 424-435). Packet reader_evidence hashes for handbook/parts/p15.tex and handbook/annex/p15.tex also differ from the current files. This audit assessed the current text.

Section 157.3 is titled '... expectation and variance in finite models', but no owed component defines or computes variance on a finite space: finite-probability.tex has no variance entry. Variance appears only in the general entries def:p15-expectation-integral and thm:p15-expectation-bounds (applicable to finite spaces through the countable-atomic formula of thm:p15-expectation-law-integral) and in non-finite examples (Var(U)=1/12, Poisson, geometric). Not a component failure; a scope-mapping question for the section.

In def:p15-convergence-failures the divergence of sum 1/(k+1) is justified by a one-sentence block remark without the block bound (2^(j-1) terms each at least 2^(-j)). The full block computation appears later on the route (annex w02b-p15-001, lines 340-344) but is not cross-referenced. Treated as elementary background; non-blocking.
In the converse of thm:p15-finite-probability-laws, passage from pair additivity to finite additivity is stated as an induction without writing the one-line inductive step. Non-blocking.

Held G&S sec. 4.1 (printed pp. 139-143) defines event independence through conditional probabilities with a null-event clause (Def 4.1; product criterion is Thm 4.1), gives an equivalent complement form of mutual independence (Def 4.2), and defines mutual independence of n random variables (Def 4.4). The handbook uses the product definition, defines random-variable independence for two variables only, and omits the n-event complement form; it proves the conditional/null-event equivalence (thm:p15-finite-independence-laws) without flagging the source's definitional choice. Outside the components' exact entries; recorded for review.

Held Durrett Step 4 (printed p. 23) defines the signed integral only for integrable f; def:p15-integrable-functions assigns a signed integral whenever one part is finite (Durrett's convention for expectations, printed p. 28). thm:p15-integral-source-bridge's 'their signed stages then agree' holds on the integrable class; the wider domain is not flagged as an extension of Durrett's sec. 1.4 integral. Non-blocking.
